findings.title: Ambient lifted vertices need not be attainable on a fixed affine slice

source_locations.detail: The proof extends the attainable-gradient interpretation to biases by homogenization and evaluation on an affine slice.

lean_locations.detail: The proved exposing point ranges over the full ambient space.

evidence: P=conv{(0,1),(2,1),(1,0)} lies in the nonnegative orthant. Its vertex (1,0) is uniquely exposed by (0,-1). On t=1 its value x is strictly less than max(1,2x+1) for every real x.
Kernel-checked lower_vertex_is_extreme and lower_vertex_below_support_on_slice in reports/evidence/attack_foundations/Counterexamples.lean.
Thus the ambient theorem remains true, while the inferred equality between all lifted vertices and gradients obtainable with the intercept fixed is false.
findings.repair: Distinguish ambient homogeneous gradients from gradients of the restricted network. For biased networks use vertices/faces exposed by allowable slice directions and project the derivatives to actual input coordinates; do not claim every lifted vertex is reachable on the slice.
findings.verdict: Concrete counterexample to the unrestricted slice inference, not to the ambient support theorem.
